batchName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395)

questions.question: How was Julian fatally wounded in Persia?
options: An arrow struck him during a siege
He fell from his horse in battle
A spear pierced his liver in a raid
He was poisoned by a Persian envoy
questions.explanation: During a Persian raid Julian rushed into the fight without his armour, and a spear pierced his liver. His doctor could not save him.
questions.sourceQuote: A spear pierced his liver, and despite his doctor's efforts he died.

questions.question: What rank did Constantius II give Julian in November 355?
questions.explanation: Julian was made a Caesar, a junior emperor, and married to Constantius' sister. He was then sent to Gaul with a small staff.
questions.sourceQuote: In November AD 355, Constantius II made his young cousin Julian a Caesar, a junior emperor, and married him to his sister.

questions.question: What distinction did Theodosius hold after his victory in 394?
options: Last emperor to live in Rome itself
First emperor born in Spain to rule Rome
Last man to rule the whole empire
questions.explanation: After winning at the river Frigidus, Theodosius ruled the entire empire, the last man ever to do so. He died at Milan in January 395.
questions.sourceQuote: He now ruled the whole empire, the last man ever to do so.

questions.question: In which city did mutinous soldiers proclaim Julian Augustus?
questions.explanation: The troops, unwilling to leave Gaul, proclaimed Julian senior emperor at Paris, then called Lutetia. By November he was openly using the title on his coins.
questions.sourceQuote: They mutinied and proclaimed Julian Augustus, senior emperor, at Paris (*Lutetia*).

questions.question: Which emperor died at the Battle of Adrianople, his body never found?
questions.explanation: Valens, emperor of the east, died in the rout and his body was never recovered. One story claims he died in a burning farmhouse.
questions.sourceQuote: Valens' body was never found; one story says he died in a burning farmhouse.

questions.question: Which people drove the Goths from their lands, prompting them to seek refuge in the empire in 376?
questions.explanation: The Huns, nomadic horsemen from the steppes, pushed the Goths out of their homeland. The Goths then asked to settle inside the Roman Empire.
questions.sourceQuote: In AD 376 the Goths, a Germanic people driven from their lands by the Huns, nomadic horsemen from the steppes, asked to settle inside the empire.

questions.question: When Rome's first Christian emperor died in AD 337, how many of his sons were proclaimed joint emperors?
questions.explanation: Three sons were proclaimed joint emperors and divided the Roman world between them. Before that, most of the old emperor's other male relatives were murdered.
questions.sourceQuote: When Rome's first Christian emperor died in AD 337, his three sons were proclaimed joint emperors and divided the Roman world between them.

questions.question: Which group was branded heretical under the Edict of Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: The Arians, who taught that the Son was created by the Father and lesser than him, were branded heretics. A council of bishops at Constantinople confirmed the official belief in 381.
questions.sourceQuote: Opponents, notably the Arians, who taught that the Son was created by the Father and lesser than him, were branded heretics.

questions.question: Where did Theodosius, made emperor in the east in 379, come from?
questions.explanation: Theodosius was a commander from Spain. His father, a famous general, had been executed in murky circumstances.
questions.sourceQuote: With Valens dead and Rome's leadership shattered, the generals turned to Theodosius, a commander from Spain whose father, a famous general, had been executed in murky circumstances.

questions.question: Where did Julian win his great victory over the Alamanni in 357?
questions.explanation: Julian's great moment came at Strasbourg, known to the Romans as Argentoratum. The heavily outnumbered Romans won overwhelmingly and captured the enemy king.
questions.sourceQuote: His great moment came in 357 at Strasbourg (*Argentoratum*).
